title: Introduction to Unix/Linux and IDBA-UD Assembly
author: Rika Anderson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jjickke

steps.title: Connect to the Remote Server
steps.instruction: Access the Liverpool Linux virtual machine using the Terminal application.

substeps.instruction: Open the Terminal application (found in Applications > Utilities).
Connect via SSH by typing: ssh [username]@liverpool.its.carleton.edu
Enter your Carleton password when prompted (note: the cursor will not move while typing).

steps.title: Verify Current Directory and Server Load
steps.instruction: Check your location in the system and monitor server resource usage to ensure proper etiquette.

substeps.instruction: Type 'pwd' to print your current working directory.
Type 'top' to view active processes and CPU/RAM usage (Liverpool has 10 CPUs and 32GB RAM).
Type 'q' to exit the top interface.

steps.title: Manage Long-Running Processes with Screen
steps.instruction: Use the screen utility to run computationally demanding processes that persist after logging off.

substeps.instruction: Type 'screen' to start a new session.
To detach from a session and leave it running in the background, press Control+A then 'd'.
To resume a detached session, type 'screen -r'.
To terminate a session, press Control+A then 'k' and confirm with 'y', or type 'exit'.

steps.title: Assemble Toy Dataset using IDBA-UD
steps.instruction: Perform a test assembly on the provided toy dataset to understand the IDBA-UD workflow.

substeps.instruction: Create a directory: mkdir toy_dataset_directory
Enter the directory: cd toy_dataset_directory
Copy the dataset: cp /usr/local/data/toy_datasets/toy_dataset_reads.fasta .
Run assembly: idba_ud -r toy_dataset_reads.fasta -o toy_assembly
Enter the output directory: cd toy_assembly
List files to verify output: ls

steps.title: Inspect Assembly Output
steps.instruction: Review the generated contigs and scaffolds.

substeps.instruction: View the final scaffold output: less scaffold.fa
Type 'q' to exit the file viewer.

steps.title: Evaluate Assembly Quality with Quast
steps.instruction: Use Quast to calculate N50 and other assembly statistics.

substeps.instruction: Run Quast on all output files: quast.py contig-20.fa contig-40.fa contig-60.fa contig-80.fa contig-100.fa scaffold.fa –o toy_assembly_quast_evaluation

steps.title: Visualize Quast Results via x2go
steps.instruction: Use the x2go client to view the HTML report of the assembly evaluation.

substeps.instruction: Open x2go and create a 'New session'.
Set Host to 'liverpool.its.carleton.edu', SSH port to 22, and session type to XFCE.
Log in with Carleton credentials.
Navigate to 'toy_assembly_quast_evaluation' and open 'report.html'.
Log out of x2go upon completion.

steps.title: Reformat Scaffold File for anvi'o
steps.instruction: Standardize the fasta file format for compatibility with anvi'o software.

substeps.instruction: Inside the assembly directory, run: anvi-script-reformat-fasta scaffold.fa -o toy_dataset_assembled.fa -l 0 --simplify-names

steps.title: Assemble Project Dataset
steps.instruction: Run the assembly process on your specific project dataset using a screen session.

substeps.instruction: Start a screen session: screen
Create and enter project directory: cd ~ && mkdir project_directory && cd project_directory
Copy your assigned dataset (e.g., cp /usr/local/data/Tara_datasets/Arabian_Sea/ERR598966_sample.fasta .)
Run assembly: idba_ud -r [your_sample].fasta -o [your_sample]_assembly
Detach from screen: Ctrl+A d

steps.title: Finalize Project Assembly Files
steps.instruction: Rename and reformat the final project assembly output.

substeps.instruction: Locate the final contig file 'contig-100.fa' (since single-end reads do not produce scaffolds).
Rename 'contig-100.fa' to '[dataset_number]_assembly.fasta' (e.g., ERR598966_assembly.fasta).
Run the reformatting script: anvi-script-reformat-fasta [your_dataset]_assembly.fasta -o [output_name].fa -l 0 --simplify-names
Ensure you have detached from any active screen sessions.
Type 'exit' to log off.
